summary: Grand County, CO summit lookout: planned in June 1912, described as an existing station by December 1912; FFLOS lists the site as abandoned.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as Abandoned; no source read describes the structure or its removal

staffing.status: planned in 1912 to be occupied by a watchman; no later staffing mentioned in sources read

facts.agency: Forest Service: Leadville National Forest in 1912; Arapaho National Forest today

events.note: June 1912: Forest Service said it intended to set up a summit station with a telephone and a watchman (a plan)
December 1912 annual report describes Williams Peak as one of three existing stations; construction date not given
A telephone line was run to the Williams Peak station during the 1912 season
January 1914 newspaper item describes the Fire Lookout station on the summit, reached by the Williams Peak trail

evidence.supports: June 1912 plan to establish a lookout station on the summit of Williams Peak
evidence.quote: They said it was the intention of the service to establish a lookout station on the summit of Williams Peak

evidence.supports: planned telephone and watchman, whose chief duty was to watch for and report fires
evidence.quote: The station is to be equipped with a telephone and to be occupied by a watchman

evidence.supports: Leadville National Forest and its assistant supervisor
evidence.quote: assistant supervisor of the Leadville National Forest

evidence.supports: three lookout stations, one on Williams Peak
evidence.quote: There are three of these stations. One is in Williams peak

evidence.supports: telephone line run to the Williams Peak station in the season
evidence.quote: A telephone line has been run to the Williams peak station during the past season.

evidence.supports: January 1914 description of the Fire Lookout station on the summit
evidence.quote: affords access to the Fire Lookout station on the summit of Williams Peak

evidence.supports: Arapaho National Forest is the current forest (page header)
summit lies in the Arapaho National Forest, 19 miles southeast of Kremmling
evidence.quote: The peak is 19 mi (31 km) southeast of Kremmling in the Arapaho National Forest

evidence.supports: Forest Service officials: S.L. Moore of the Forest Service Denver office went with the assistant supervisor
evidence.quote: S.L. Moore, of the Denver office of the Forest Service

evidence.supports: plan reported in the June 28, 1912 item
watchman's chief duty: look out for and report fires
evidence.quote: whose chief duty will be to look out for and report anything that looks like a real or threatened forest fire

evidence.supports: annual report of the assistant supervisor describing the stations
evidence.quote: Assistant Supervisor Robert E. Clark's annual report

evidence.supports: view from the station over Grand County and parts of Summit and Routt counties
evidence.quote: From here one can see practically all of Grand county, the northern half of Summit and the southern portion of Routt county

corrections.why: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists the site as Abandoned; no source read says the structure was removed or destroyed

notes_for_editor: No source after 1914 was found about the lookout, its fate or what is at the summit today. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list gives no date for the abandonment. The Colorado Fire Lookout Tower Collection finding aid (historycolorado.org Mss.02651 PDF) was not read and may cover this site. NHLR does not list it. Brief status 'gone' was changed to 'abandoned' because the source does not say the structure is gone.
